correctness.rationale: Let \(g(t)=t^{2}-t+1\). For a counterexample with \(2\le a<b\), the positive integer \(z=g(a)/b\) satisfies \(z<a\) and \(bz\equiv1\pmod a\); therefore \(z^{2}g(b)\equiv g(z)\pmod a\), producing a smaller reciprocal pair or the impossible case \(z=1\). Minimal-maximum descent proves the global theorem. Multiplicativity gives \(\mathcal H(n)=\prod_{p\mid n}g(p)/n\) for squarefree \(n\); the finite prime graph has an outgoing edge at every vertex and hence a cycle of length at least three. The explicit witness consists of three primes verified by exact trial division and cyclic congruences. Finite verification is supplementary, not proof of the unbounded claim.

originality.rationale: De Koninck–Letendre, arXiv:2610.10572v1, Section 5, Proposition 1, provides an \(O(z^{1/3}/(\log z)^2)\) count for odd-prime reciprocal-divisibility systems but no exclusion theorem. The new no-two-cycle descent over all integers is strictly stronger for the first-power two-cycle subsystem, and yields a sharp squarefree support corollary. OEIS A317480 supplies a computational catalogue, not this structural obstruction. Targeted published-finding and literature searches retrieved no dominating result. Priority remains subject to unindexed earlier elementary proofs.

value.rationale: The theorem eliminates completely a substantive first-power/first-power two-cycle case in an October 2026 analytic-number-theory paper, rather than only improving a counting constant. Its all-integer statement gives the sharp bound \(\omega(n)\ge3\) for nontrivial squarefree inputs with integral reciprocal-gcd sums, extending the source's \(\omega(n)\ge2\) fact. This is a structural mathematical classification with a motivated application, not the rediscovery of the explicit known witness.
